edges.description: The remaining wild-type allele is lost somatically in the cell that goes on to transform. Biallelic inactivation of BRCA1, BRCA2 or PALB2 is documented in a fifth of breast cancer brain metastases, which is evidence the second hit occurs rather than a measurement of how often it does in primary carrier tumours.
With both alleles inactivated the scaffold is absent and the BRCA1 to BRCA2-RAD51 bridge cannot be assembled.

edges.description: Breast epithelium is the dominant site, at 53% absolute risk to age 80.
Ovarian cancer is elevated about threefold but at low absolute risk.
Pancreatic cancer is elevated about twofold, at 2-3% absolute risk to age 80.
The knockout establishes that Palb2 is essential for development, which supports the genome-maintenance role, but the heterozygote that corresponds to the human carrier is normal and fertile.
edges.limitations: Homozygous loss is embryonic lethal at E9.5, so the adult tumour phenotype cannot be observed in the constitutive model; the heterozygote, which is the genotype matching the human disease, is normal and fertile and develops no reported tumour phenotype in the cited work. Conditional or tissue-specific models are required.

nodes.description: Female breast cancer is the dominant manifestation, at a relative risk of 7.18 and an absolute risk of 53% to age 80. Absolute risk is strongly modified: the consortium range runs from about 44% to 76% depending on family history and polygenic background, so a single figure overstates what can be told an individual carrier. Tumours are enriched for oestrogen-receptor-negative disease, and in an ascertained cohort of women diagnosed at 40 or younger the panel positivity rate was higher in triple-negative and bilateral tumours. Onset is adult, with enrichment at young ages.

nodes.description: A heterozygous germline protein-truncating variant halves functional PALB2 in every cell. PALB2 is a modular scaffold: its N-terminal coiled-coil homodimerizes and binds the BRCA1 coiled-coil, while its C-terminal WD40 beta-propeller binds BRCA2, RAD51 and RAD51C, so the protein has no catalytic activity of its own and its loss is felt as a failure to assemble a complex. ClinGen records the disease mechanism as loss of function.

nodes.description: Error-prone repair in place of homologous recombination produces chromosome fragility, hypersensitivity to interstrand-crosslinking agents and ionizing radiation, and progressive genomic instability. This is simultaneously the route to malignancy and the therapeutic vulnerability the disease is treated through.

nodes.description: Homologous-recombination deficiency makes the tumour synthetically lethal to PARP inhibition. This is not an inference from the mechanism: in the TBCRC 048 phase II study of olaparib across homologous-recombination genes, confirmed responses were seen only in germline PALB2 and somatic BRCA1/2 carriers, and the PALB2 group had the highest objective response rate and the longest median progression-free survival, while ATM and CHEK2 carriers had none. The expansion cohorts then reproduced the effect in 24 germline PALB2 patients at a 75% objective response rate and a 9.4-month median progression-free survival, the larger of the two PALB2 series. Platinum sensitivity is deliberately not claimed on this node: it is mechanistically expected and is standard care in the associated cancers, but no source cached for this entry reports a platinum result in PALB2 carriers specifically, and the node is named for what the evidence covers.

nodes.description: Olaparib in metastatic breast cancer with a germline PALB2 variant. In the initial TBCRC 048 cohorts the germline PALB2 arm had an objective response rate of 82% and a median progression-free survival of 13.3 months, the strongest result in the trial, while ATM and CHEK2 carriers had no responses. The trial's later expansion cohorts, 24 germline PALB2 patients, are the larger series: an objective response rate of 75% and a median progression-free survival of 9.4 months.

nodes.description: Homozygous Palb2 null mice are embryonic lethal by E9.5, phenocopying Brca1 and Brca2 knockouts, while heterozygotes are normal and fertile. The heterozygote is therefore the genotype that matches the human carrier state, and it has no phenotype, so the model cannot be used to study the dominant cancer predisposition without conditional or tissue-specific approaches.
Pancreatic cancer is elevated about twofold with an absolute risk to age 80 of 2-3%. This is the risk on which family-history-triggered pancreatic surveillance is offered.

nodes.description: Imaging surveillance of the pancreas, offered to PALB2 heterozygotes as high-risk individuals. In the PRECEDE prospective cohort, PALB2 carriers were 9% of the 2,085 eligible participants and baseline imaging was predominantly endoscopic ultrasound or MRI. The evidence base is thin by the consortium's own account: it reports that limited evidence exists to guide counselling on how often to image and what the findings mean over time, so this row records an offered programme rather than a demonstrated mortality benefit.
